editorial.description_en: The palest warm off-white in the corpus, a shade away from paper white. It carries just enough yellow to stop the eye reading it as blue-white.
editorial.description_ja: 紙のようにうすく、わずかに黄みをおびた白。
editorial.contemporaryNote_en: The lightest ground the product will put a swatch on. Anything paler stops being a colour and becomes the page.

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.962, C 0.006, h 92.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 薄 (usu, thin) + 紙 (kami, paper), rendaku to -gami. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Thin Paper" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 薄紙. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — kai-jiro at ΔE00 2.3, usu-shimo at ΔE00 4.3, asa-nuno at ΔE00 5.3. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.006 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
